dedupe_keys.name: aims spatial flood defences including standardised attributes

description: AIMS Spatial Flood Defences is the Environment Agency's national layer of flood and coastal defences in England, and the Agency describes it as the only complete and up-to-date dataset showing the defences it currently owns, manages or inspects. A defence is any asset that provides flood defence or coastal protection, man-made or natural: typically earth banks, stone and concrete walls or sheet piling, and also structures, buildings or parts of buildings, which usually work together within a risk management system. Each asset is a vector feature with standardised attributes explained in a product description document. It is taken from the Agency's asset information management system (product AfA345) and updated daily. Coverage is England, in British National Grid. The full national dataset can be downloaded as GeoPackage, GeoJSON, shapefile or file geodatabase from the Defra Data Services Platform, which warns that the download can take seven to eight minutes, and the record states no public access constraints under the Open Government Licence, free of charge. Caveats: defences owned by others and not inspected by the Agency are not necessarily included, and a retired version without standardised attributes should no longer be used. Simulation uses: system description for flood-defence failure and breach models, hazard exposure behind defences, resilience and climate adaptation planning. It pairs with the Agency's Risk of Flooding from Surface Water map (data-ea-risk-of-flooding-from-surface-water).
